office_does: The sheriff runs county law enforcement and the county jail, serves warrants and court orders, and in Grant County also directs emergency management.
race_blurb: First-term Sheriff Joey Kriete faces Moses Lake police Sgt. Darrik Gregg, a former chief deputy who narrowly led the primary; both prefer the Republican Party. The race has turned on leadership inside the office, including a deputies' no-confidence vote, Kriete's demotion of a rival candidate and Gregg's pending lawsuit against the county.

candidates.summary: Moses Lake police patrol sergeant and former Grant County chief deputy with about 23 years in law enforcement, running on servant leadership, accountability and a fresh approach to the office.
highlights: Says he is 'tough on crime while treating people with respect and dignity' and will hold criminals accountable [S1]
Would conduct a comprehensive review of staffing, policies, response times and spending in his first six months [S11]
Would continue his federal retaliation lawsuit against the county if elected [S8]
Endorsed by the Moses Lake Police Officer's Guild [S3]

experience.basis: Career officer and former chief deputy who has never held elected office and argues the county needs a fresh approach to leadership.

safety.basis: Enforcement framing ('tough on crime', 'hold criminals accountable', support for Flock cameras) alongside community-partnership language; no specific treatment or diversion proposals.

candidates.summary: Incumbent sheriff since 2023 with more than three decades in the Grant County Sheriff's Office, running on restaffing, proactive policing and state accreditation.
highlights: Created a Crime Reduction Team targeting property crime and theft, including in rural farming areas [S1]
Cites expanded mental-health response and behavioral-health and opioid partnerships [S1][S12]
Would protect core services and keep operations financially sustainable as the new jail opens [S10]
Says the deputies' association gave no details behind its no-confidence vote by his deadline [S7]

experience.basis: First-term incumbent with 32 years in the office before election, WASPC vice president, who asks voters to judge his record.

safety.basis: Proactive policing, a property-crime unit and federal cooperation on criminal cases, paired with expanded mental-health response and recovery pathways.

spending.basis: Says he will keep operations financially sustainable and may say no to programs, positions or equipment.
